quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may get frustrated and make unsafe moves to pass you. It is safest to drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit.

questions.question: To avoid losing grip on wet roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas. Do not brake. Keep the vehicle straight and let it slow down.

questions.question: Speeding:

options.text: Helps you react faster to danger.

questions.explanation: Speeding is a top cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the arrow's direction if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the right lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the right lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you may go in that direction when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean passing is:
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the posted speed limit based on conditions, but never faster. Slow down for curves, hills with limited sight, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with traffic going both ways.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Even with proper mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: Stopping distance and crash severity:
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the worse crashes become.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downhill road ahead. Check your brakes before going down.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Locks the front wheels, so you cannot steer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, so you cannot steer.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels. This stops you from steering. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid needing hard braking.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check behind you. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also check that no one is trying to move into the same spot from another lane.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should:
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must look over your shoulders to see into your blind spots.

questions.question: A truck's blind spots are:

options.text: On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots are much larger than car blind spots. The driver cannot see your car behind the truck. If you are behind or beside a truck and cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after you stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. You should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.explanation: When it is dark and hard to see, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can see the road ahead again. Move back into your lane only when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: A major cause of fatal traffic accidents in Tennessee is:
questions.explanation: Driving faster than the safe and legal speed limit is a major cause of fatal traffic accidents in Tennessee.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work areas have:

options.text: A red background with green writing.
An orange background with black writing.
A yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the road edge. If your brakes fail, the car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: A bad suspension system can cause:
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns of danger ahead. Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: Which statement describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no mercy and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting possible mistakes from other drivers and being ready to respond to them.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead helps you:
questions.explanation: Look far ahead on the road to avoid last-minute braking or turning. By watching ahead, you can drive more safely, use less fuel, and help traffic move at a steady speed.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows down all nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and hurts your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events:

options.text: Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.explanation: Avoid staring at accidents or unusual events. This practice, called rubbernecking, causes traffic to slow down and creates congestion.

questions.question: If you park in an area not normally used for parking:

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from any direction.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from any direction.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked car does not become a hazard. Wherever you park, other drivers must be able to see your vehicle from any direction.

questions.question: You can help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed to help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away. Also signal your turns, lane changes, and slowdowns in advance.
